name: Fjord Intranet
role: clean control (Fixture E): no seeded vulnerability; measures false positives
functionality: login form with a session-bound CSRF token (POST /login) and JSON login (POST /api/session); logout (POST /logout, DELETE /api/session)
dashboard with status message, pending leave count and announcements
staff directory with search and pagination (/directory, /api/directory?q=&page=&per_page=)
personal leave requests: list (paginated), detail, create (/leave, /leave/{id}, /api/leave, /api/leave/{id}, POST /api/leave)
leave approval for HR admins only (POST /api/leave/{id}/approve, /api/admin/leave, /admin)
team documents restricted to the caller's team (/teams, /api/teams/{team}/documents[/{doc}])
profile view and edit of harmless fields only (/profile, GET/PATCH /api/me)

data_only_accounts.note: password is random per process and never handed out; owns leave 304/310 and payslip d7a0c3f6-...

login.body: form with csrf token (also JSON at /api/session)
login.csrf: GET /login sets an anonymous fjord_session pre-session and renders hidden input csrf_token bound to it; POST /login (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) must echo it. On success the session id is rotated and the response is 303 to a validated same-site 'next' (default /dashboard). Alternative: POST /api/session with Content-Type application/json {username,password} (no token; JSON-only + same-origin Origin check + no CORS). After login every state change needs header X-CSRF-Token equal to the session token, available in <meta name="csrf-token"> on every page and from GET /api/session.

resources.control: ownership; others' ids return the same 404 as non-existent ids
membership; other or unknown team -> 403; a document requested under the wrong team -> 404
role admin only -> 403 for employees (role checked before lookup)
CSRF + only status_message (<=140), pronouns (<=20), office_location (Bergen|Oslo|Tromsø|Remote); any other key (role, team, email ...) -> 400
CSRF + owner is always the session user; only start, end, kind, note accepted; status always pending

design_choices.what: staff directory exposes colleagues' name, team, title, office extension and work e-mail to all signed-in employees
design_choices.why: intended intranet feature; requires authentication; no private data (no home address, salary, personal phone)
crawler hint only; /admin is authenticated and role-checked

design_choices.what: ETag on static assets and API responses, random X-Request-Id on every response
design_choices.why: caching and support correlation; neither carries sensitive data
monitoring and client compatibility; no versions, hosts or build data

design_choices.what: other users' leave ids / payslip ids and non-existent ids return the same 404
design_choices.why: deliberate: hides existence; sequential leave ids are not a weakness because ownership is enforced

design_choices.what: unknown teams and other teams both answer 403 on team documents
design_choices.why: membership check before lookup; team names are public via the directory anyway

design_choices.what: OPTIONS answers 204 with an Allow header and no Access-Control-* headers
JSON login (POST /api/session) needs no CSRF token
design_choices.why: JSON content type is mandatory (cross-site requires a preflight that is never granted), a foreign Origin is rejected with 403, cookie is SameSite=Strict

design_choices.what: per-account lockout after 10 consecutive failures for 15 minutes, with the same generic message
design_choices.why: brute-force protection without user enumeration (unknown usernames behave identically)

lab_artefacts.what: session cookie fjord_session without the Secure flag (and not __Host- prefixed) because the lab is plain http on loopback; production would set Secure
no Strict-Transport-Security header and no TLS, because the lab is plain http on loopback (HSTS over http is ignored by browsers)

negative_controls.truth: ownership enforced: sofia gets 404 for jonas's 302 and his payslips, byte-identical to non-existent ids
membership enforced: other and unknown teams -> 403; doc under wrong team -> 404
admin role enforced; employees get 403, anonymous users are redirected to /login (pages) or get 401 (API)
no Access-Control-Allow-Origin / -Credentials for any Origin, including preflights

negative_controls.where: all responses (HTML, API, static, errors, OPTIONS)
negative_controls.truth: CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP/CORP present; no Server / X-Powered-By
Disallow: /admin is a crawler hint; /admin is protected (DC2)
generic errors without stack traces; minimal health/version; public config only (DC3-DC5)

negative_controls.where: PATCH /api/me, POST /api/leave, POST /api/leave/{id}/approve, DELETE /api/session, POST /login, POST /logout, POST /api/session
negative_controls.truth: session-bound CSRF token required (header X-CSRF-Token or form csrf_token) plus same-origin Origin check; JSON login protected per DC9
all output HTML-escaped; CSP script-src 'self' without inline scripts
next accepts only same-site paths ('//', '\\', absolute URLs fall back to /dashboard)
generic error for unknown user and wrong password, session id rotated on login, lockout after 10 failures (DC10)
unknown fields (role, team, owner, status ...) rejected with 400; owner always the session user

expected_observations: both accounts sign in (form with CSRF token, or JSON /api/session) and receive a rotated HttpOnly SameSite=Strict fjord_session cookie
sofia's and jonas's leave and payslip ids are mutually inaccessible (404 identical to non-existent)
team documents are visible only for the caller's own team (403 otherwise)
/admin and admin APIs answer 403 to both accounts
state-changing requests without a valid X-CSRF-Token are rejected with 403
no CORS headers for a foreign Origin, including preflights
strict security headers on every response; no Server / X-Powered-By
directory shows colleagues' work contact details by design
the cookie lacks Secure and there is no HSTS only because the lab is plain http (LA1, LA2)

fp_policy.note: any verified finding of class vulnerability or misconfiguration is a false positive; hardening/informational findings are reviewed manually for accuracy (LA1/LA2 are acceptable)
